parameters.name: supply_voltage
parameters.description: Operating DC supply voltage range within which all AC and DC parameters are guaranteed. The device must be powered within this range for reliable operation. Voltage grade is often encoded in the part number suffix (e.g. Microchip 24AA=1.7V, 24LC=2.5V, ST M24128-R=1.8V, M24128-W=2.5V).
parameters.notes: Candidate VCC range must fully contain base chip VCC range. Example: base 1.8-5.5V, candidate must support at minimum 1.8-5.5V.

parameters.name: operating_temperature
parameters.description: Ambient air temperature range over which all DC and AC specifications are guaranteed.
parameters.notes: Candidate temperature range must be equal to or wider than base chip temperature range. A -40 to +125C part covers a -40 to +85C base.

parameters.name: max_clock_frequency
parameters.description: Maximum allowed SCL clock frequency at which all AC and DC parameters are guaranteed. Determines the highest I2C bus speed the device supports: Standard-mode 100 kHz, Fast-mode 400 kHz, Fast-mode Plus 1 MHz.
parameters.notes: Candidate fC(max) must be >= base fC(max). System operates at the frequency the base chip supports; the replacement must handle at least that same speed. Higher max capability is a strict superset — always safe.

parameters.name: input_high_voltage
parameters.description: Minimum voltage that must be applied to an input pin (SCL, SDA, WC/WP, E0-E2) for the chip to recognise it as a logic HIGH level. Typically specified as a fraction of VCC.
parameters.notes: Candidate VIH(min) must be <= base VIH(min). A lower HIGH threshold means the chip is more tolerant of weaker drive signals. Practically: most vendors specify 0.7xVCC, so this rarely differentiates.

parameters.name: input_low_voltage
parameters.description: Maximum voltage at an input pin (SCL, SDA, WC/WP, E0-E2) that is still recognised as a logic LOW.
parameters.notes: Candidate VIL(max) must be >= base VIL(max). A higher VIL(max) means the chip accepts a higher voltage as LOW — more tolerant. Practically: most vendors specify 0.3xVCC, so this rarely differentiates.

parameters.name: input_hysteresis_voltage
parameters.description: Voltage hysteresis of the Schmitt trigger inputs on SCL and SDA. Provides noise immunity by requiring signals to move by this amount before a logic level transition is recognised. Not all vendors specify this explicitly.
parameters.notes: Candidate VHYS(min) must be >= base VHYS(min). Greater hysteresis provides more noise immunity. Microchip 24FC128 explicitly specifies 0.05xVCC; ST M24128 does not list a separate VHYS symbol.

parameters.name: output_low_voltage
parameters.description: Maximum SDA output pin voltage when the EEPROM is sinking the specified load current at logic LOW (open-drain output). Applies when the device drives ACK or read data.
parameters.notes: Candidate VOL(max) must be <= base VOL(max). Candidate must pull SDA at least as low as the base chip under equivalent load current. Typical: 0.4V max at IOL = 3 mA across all vendors.

parameters.name: supply_current_read
parameters.description: Maximum current drawn from the VCC supply during active read operation with SCL clocking at the rated frequency. Atmel and Rohm use ICC1 for read current in a numbered ICC1/ICC2 convention.
parameters.notes: Candidate ICC read(max) must be <= base ICC read(max). Atmel AT24C128C and Rohm BR24G128 use ICC1 for read current (ICC2 for write) — important deviation from standard naming.

parameters.name: supply_current_write
parameters.description: Maximum current drawn from the VCC supply during the internal write cycle after the STOP condition. Atmel and Rohm use ICC2 for write current in a numbered ICC1/ICC2 convention.
parameters.notes: Candidate ICC write(max) must be <= base ICC write(max). Atmel AT24C128C and Rohm BR24G128 use ICC2 for write current — pair with ICC1 for read current.

parameters.name: standby_current
parameters.description: Quiescent current drawn from VCC when the device is in standby mode: not selected, no I2C activity, all inputs static. ST/ON Semi/Renesas use ICCS; Microchip/Atmel use ISB — two separate symbols for the same parameter.
parameters.notes: Candidate standby current(max) must be <= base standby current(max). CRITICAL SYMBOL NOTE: ST (ICCS) and Microchip/Atmel (ISB) use completely different symbols for this parameter. Both must be aliased.

parameters.name: scl_clock_high_time
parameters.description: Minimum time SCL must remain at logic HIGH within one clock cycle. Together with tLOW determines maximum clock frequency and duty cycle. The I2C bus master must sustain SCL HIGH for at least this duration. Rohm uses tSCLH instead of the standard tHIGH.
parameters.notes: Candidate tHIGH(min) must be <= base tHIGH(min). Bus master provides a fixed HIGH time designed for the base chip; the replacement must work with a shorter HIGH period. VENDOR NOTE: Rohm uses tSCLH (unique); ISSI uses tH as shorthand.

parameters.name: scl_clock_low_time
parameters.description: Minimum time SCL must remain at logic LOW within one clock cycle. The I2C bus master must hold SCL LOW for at least this duration to allow data setup and hold on SDA. Rohm uses tSCLL instead of the standard tLOW.
parameters.notes: Candidate tLOW(min) must be <= base tLOW(min). VENDOR NOTE: Rohm uses tSCLL (unique); ISSI uses tL as shorthand.

parameters.name: scl_sda_rise_time
parameters.description: Maximum allowable rise time of SCL and SDA signals, measured from 0.3xVCC to 0.7xVCC. Determined by bus pull-up resistor and line capacitance. The device must tolerate signals rising up to this speed.
aliases: rise time of SDA and SCL signals
rise time of both SDA and SCL
parameters.notes: Candidate tR(max) must be >= base tR(max). More tolerance for slow rising edges means safe in the existing bus RC environment. Symbol tR is the most consistent across all EEPROM vendors.

parameters.name: scl_sda_fall_time
parameters.description: Maximum allowable fall time of SCL and SDA INPUT signals, measured from 0.7xVCC to 0.3xVCC. The device must tolerate signals falling up to this speed. Note: some datasheets list a SEPARATE tOF for the SDA output driver — see sda_output_fall_time.
aliases: fall time of SDA and SCL signals
fall time of both SDA and SCL
parameters.notes: Candidate input tF(max) must be >= base input tF(max). More tolerance for slow falling edges is safe. IMPORTANT: Microchip 24FC128 does NOT separate input tF from output tF — a single tF row covers both. ST M24128 lists them separately.

parameters.name: sda_output_fall_time
parameters.description: Maximum fall time of the SDA output signal when the EEPROM drives SDA LOW (open-drain output). Relevant during read data and ACK transmissions. Affects signal integrity at higher bus speeds. Microchip merges this with general tF; ST and newer Atmel list it separately as tOF.
aliases: SDA fall time from VIH to VIL
output fall time from VIH(min) to VIL(max)
parameters.notes: Candidate SDA output tF(max) must be <= base tF(max). A slower output fall (higher value) risks signal integrity issues at high frequencies. When only a single tF row appears in the datasheet (Microchip pattern), it covers both input and output.

parameters.name: data_setup_time
parameters.description: Minimum time SDA data must be stable and valid before the rising edge of SCL during data transfer. The I2C bus master ensures this setup time when writing data or address bytes. ON Semiconductor uses tDS instead of tSU:DAT.
aliases: data valid before SCL rising edge
parameters.notes: Candidate tSU:DAT(min) must be <= base tSU:DAT(min). SEPARATOR NOTE: ON Semi uses tSU.DAT (period); NXP UM10204 spec uses tSU;DAT (semicolon). All are the same parameter. SYMBOL NOTE: ON Semi and ISSI use tDS as a short form.

parameters.name: data_hold_time
parameters.description: Minimum time SDA data must remain stable after the falling edge of SCL to avoid generating a spurious START or STOP condition. The I2C bus master maintains this hold time. ON Semiconductor and ISSI use tDH instead of tHD:DAT.
aliases: data valid after SCL falling edge
parameters.notes: Candidate tHD:DAT(min) must be <= base tHD:DAT(min). SEPARATOR NOTE: ON Semi uses tHD.DAT (period); NXP UM10204 uses tHD;DAT. SYMBOL NOTE: ON Semi and ISSI use tDH as a short form. Many datasheets specify 0 ns minimum for this parameter.

parameters.name: data_out_hold_time
parameters.description: Minimum time the EEPROM holds valid output data on SDA stable after the falling edge of SCL during read operations. This is a chip guarantee to the bus master — the system relies on SDA remaining valid for at least this duration.
aliases: output data hold after SCL low
data valid hold from SCL fall
SDA valid hold after SCL fall
parameters.notes: Candidate tDH(min) must be >= base tDH(min). The system relies on the EEPROM holding data valid for at least this time after SCL falls. ST uses tDH symbol for this; note symbol overlap with ON Semi's tDH meaning input data hold — distinguish by context (transmitter vs. receiver role).

parameters.name: output_valid_from_clock
parameters.description: Maximum time from the falling edge of SCL to when valid data is guaranteed on SDA for read operations. This is the I2C EEPROM equivalent of access time. Also known as tVD;DAT in the NXP UM10204 I2C specification.
aliases: SCL fall to SDA data valid
parameters.notes: Candidate tAA(max) must be <= base tAA(max). Replacement must deliver data at least as fast within the SCL clock period. tAA is the most consistent symbol across all EEPROM vendors. NXP UM10204 I2C spec uses tVD;DAT for this same measurement.

parameters.name: start_condition_setup_time
parameters.description: Minimum time from a rising edge of SCL to the falling edge of SDA that generates a (repeated) START condition. Rohm uses tSSU instead of the standard tSU:STA.
aliases: SCL high to SDA low START
setup time for repeated START condition
set-up time for a repeated START condition
parameters.notes: Candidate tSU:STA(min) must be <= base tSU:STA(min). SEPARATOR NOTE: ON Semi uses tSU.STA (period); NXP UM10204 uses tSU;STA. SYMBOL NOTE: Rohm uses tSSU (completely different symbol — high matching risk).

parameters.name: start_condition_hold_time
parameters.description: Minimum time after the SDA falling edge of a START condition before SCL can go LOW for the first clock pulse. Ensures reliable START detection by all devices. Rohm uses tSHD instead of the standard tHD:STA.
aliases: SDA falling to SCL falling START
parameters.notes: Candidate tHD:STA(min) must be <= base tHD:STA(min). SEPARATOR NOTE: ON Semi uses tHD.STA (period); NXP UM10204 uses tHD;STA. SYMBOL NOTE: Rohm uses tSHD (completely different symbol — highest matching risk in this parameter group).

parameters.name: stop_condition_setup_time
parameters.description: Minimum time SCL must remain HIGH before the rising edge of SDA that generates the STOP condition. Rohm uses tSSTO; ON Semi uses tSTO (drops SU: prefix); legacy Catalyst used tPSU.
aliases: SCL high before SDA rising STOP
parameters.notes: Candidate tSU:STO(min) must be <= base tSU:STO(min). SYMBOL NOTES: ON Semi uses tSTO (no SU prefix — significant divergence); Rohm uses tSSTO; legacy Catalyst Semiconductor used tPSU.

parameters.name: bus_free_time
parameters.description: Minimum time the I2C bus must remain free (SDA and SCL both HIGH) between a STOP condition and a new START condition. Ensures all bus devices have released the bus before a new transaction begins.
aliases: STOP condition to START condition time
bus free time between a STOP and START condition
parameters.notes: Candidate tBUF(min) must be <= base tBUF(min). tBUF is the most consistent symbol across all I2C EEPROM vendors — very low matching ambiguity.

parameters.name: input_spike_suppression
parameters.description: Maximum width of a noise spike on SCL or SDA that is filtered and suppressed by the device's built-in input filter. Pulses shorter than this value are ignored. Rohm uses tNF; old Atmel used tNS (easily confused with the unit nanoseconds).
aliases: pulse width ignored on SCL SDA
parameters.notes: Candidate tSP(max) must be >= base tSP(max). More aggressive filtering provides at least the same noise immunity. CRITICAL SYMBOL WARNINGS: (1) Old Atmel used tNS for this parameter — do NOT confuse with the unit 'ns'; if 'tNS' appears as a row header in a timing table, it is this parameter. (2) Rohm uses tNF (noise filter time). Both must be aliased.

parameters.name: wp_setup_time
parameters.description: Minimum time the Write Protect (WP / WC) pin must be at the required stable level before the Start condition of a write instruction. Many vendors do not list a formal timing symbol — check both the AC table and the operational description.
parameters.notes: Candidate tSU:WP(min) must be <= base tSU:WP(min). IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE: ST M24128 specifies 0 ns (no setup required); Microchip 24FC128 specifies 600 ns — this will correctly flag NOT OK if comparing them. Many vendors do not list WP timing at all; treat absent spec as 'no constraint'.

parameters.name: wp_hold_time
parameters.description: Minimum time the Write Protect (WP / WC) pin must remain at the required stable level after the Stop condition of a write instruction. Many vendors do not list this parameter formally.
parameters.notes: Candidate tHD:WP(min) must be <= base tHD:WP(min). ST M24128 specifies 1 us; Microchip 24FC128 specifies 1.3 us — candidate requires MORE hold time than the system was designed for, correctly flagging NOT OK.

parameters.name: write_cycle_time
parameters.description: Maximum time required for the device to complete one internal EEPROM programming cycle after the STOP condition. Device is busy (NACK) during this period. ST uses tW; Microchip uses tWC; Atmel/Rohm use tWR — three different symbols for the same parameter across the major vendors.
parameters.notes: Candidate tW(max) must be <= base tW(max). Firmware waits up to tW(base) before ACK polling or next command; a slower candidate will be accessed prematurely. CRITICAL SYMBOL NOTE: ST uses 'tW' (all M24 family); Microchip uses 'tWC'; Atmel/Rohm use 'tWR'. This ST vs. industry difference is the single highest-risk symbol collision in EEPROM write parameters.

parameters.name: write_endurance
parameters.description: Minimum guaranteed number of erase/write cycles per memory cell over the operating temperature range. Typically in a separate Reliability or Memory Characteristics table, NOT in the AC timing table. Most vendors do not use a short symbol for this — it appears as prose or a table row header.
parameters.notes: Candidate write endurance must be >= base. Typical values: 1,000,000 cycles (Microchip, Atmel, ON Semi, ISSI, Rohm); 4,000,000 cycles (ST M24128 at TA=25C). LOCATION NOTE: This parameter is almost always in a reliability/endurance table, never the AC timing table.

parameters.name: data_retention
parameters.description: Minimum guaranteed time that data stored in the EEPROM is retained without power after the last write cycle. Always in the Reliability or Memory Characteristics section, not the AC timing table. Typical values range from 10 years (legacy NXP) to 200 years (ST, Microchip).
parameters.notes: Candidate data retention must be >= base. ST M24128 and Microchip 24LC128 both specify 200 years. NOTE: NXP PCF8582 (legacy) specifies only 10 years — dramatically different; would correctly flag NOT OK vs. a 200-year base device.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Size of the internal write page buffer in bytes. A page write can transfer up to this many bytes in a single cycle. If more bytes are sent, the address counter wraps within the page boundary causing data corruption. This parameter is almost always in prose (Device Operation section), NOT in a formal parameter table.
parameters.notes: Candidate page size must be >= base page size. Firmware written for the base chip sends up to page_size bytes per write; a smaller candidate buffer causes data rollover and corruption without any error. Standard for 128-Kbit family: 64 bytes (ST, Microchip, Atmel, ON Semi, ISSI, Rohm, Renesas). EXCEPTION: NXP PCF8582 uses 16 bytes — critical incompatibility. LOCATION NOTE: Almost always in prose ('Device Operation', 'Memory Organization'), never in the AC timing table.
